title: The medieval saints, again
tomorrow: what does a Church that's always in need of renewal fix first?

lines: A RICH KID, A RUNAWAY, A PREACHER.
cards: A contacts list keeps people you haven't texted in years, and you could still call any of them. Catholics talk about saints that way. Four of the old ones: Francis, a cloth merchant's son who gave everything away.

Clare, who, tradition says, slipped out of her family's house at night to follow him. Dominic, a preacher who founded an order of preachers. And Catherine of Siena, who wrote fearless letters, even to a pope.

teach.b: Each one is a friend for a different day, and each one wears a carry from this week. Dominic sent his brothers out two by two to preach: sent.
Francis called the sun his brother and the moon his sister in his Canticle of the Creatures, a man fully alive to every creature God made.
Clare stayed put in one small convent for the rest of her life and kept her sisters steady with a patience that never fell away.

Catherine told a pope what the Church needed, out loud and in writing, because she believed the Church could be made new. Something to tell a friend tonight: Catholics don't treat these four as statues.
The Creed calls it the communion of saints: the friends who already climbed the hill are still part of the family, and they pray with the rest of us.

how: Catholics keep the feasts of Francis, Clare, Dominic and Catherine of Siena in the Church's calendar, and many pick a saint as a patron at confirmation and ask that saint's prayers.

monks who copied old books by candlelight

games.q: your little cousin asks at dinner why Catholics talk to saints who died long ago. what's a sentence a parent could say?
o: saints are old friends who finished the climb and still pray with us.
saints are lesser gods that Catholics worship alongside God.
saints only matter because they did well-known miracles.
games.why: Catholics honor the saints and ask their prayers, the communion of saints in the Creed; worship belongs to God alone.

practice: Count four old friends on your fingers: Francis, Clare, Dominic, Catherine. Pick the one you need this week, and say the name once more, slowly. For the sit, keep that one company the way you'd sit beside a friend, no words needed.

wordCard.voice: The medieval saints. Francis, Clare, Dominic and Catherine: old friends Catholics still turn to, centuries on.

orig.note: Latin: peace and good, a greeting Franciscans use, credited by tradition to Francis.

carryVoice: Your line: old friends. A saint is a friend who already climbed the hill. Two weeks done, see you tomorrow.
